quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving is to:

options.text: Pay attention to what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention to what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle. Look to the front, sides, and rear. This helps you spot problems early so you can change your speed or position when needed.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Faster speeds make crashes more likely to be fatal.
Faster speeds mean you need more space between cars.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. Above 80 miles per hour, survival is unlikely. Faster speeds also require longer stopping distances, so you need to stay farther from the car ahead.

questions.question: When driving at high speeds, signal ____ before changing lanes or turning.

options.text: One second
Two to three seconds
Four to five seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Four to five seconds
questions.explanation: You must use turn signals before changing lanes or turning. At high speeds, signal four to five seconds before you turn or change lanes.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered railroad gate. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: You can legally turn left at a red light after stopping only if:

options.text: You are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.
You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. There must be no sign prohibiting this turn.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You can only turn left onto another one-way street if:

options.text: You increase your speed before the turn.
Traffic on that street moves to the right.
Traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left if there is no sign prohibiting it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are what color?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws. They show rules about direction, lanes, turning, speed, parking, and special situations. These signs are usually white rectangles with black, red, or green text or pictures.

questions.question: When parking uphill with no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the road edge.
Turn your wheels away from the road edge.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, turn your front wheels right toward the road edge. This stops the car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for them if you can.
Speed up to keep your spot.
Always stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for them if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room to let merging vehicles enter your lane.

questions.question: When you see a yield sign, you should first:

options.text: Look for cross traffic.
Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Look for cross traffic when you approach a yield sign. If there is traffic, you may need to stop and wait before merging onto the road.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red traffic signal?

options.text: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and go carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can drive in either direction in this lane.
Traffic is coming from both directions.
You are near a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is coming from both directions.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming from both directions.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an octagonal sign?

options.text: Slow down.
Stop.
Turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop, let traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which one is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every two to five seconds to see what is around you. Staring straight ahead is unsafe. In fog, use low beam lights, not high beams.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and go carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights and a siren is approaching while you are in an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull right and stop before leaving the intersection.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. You must always yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A yield sign is ahead.
A road is joining from the left.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yield sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start slowing down when you see this sign.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A flagger is ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mean there is work zone activity. When you see orange signs, stay alert for unexpected driving conditions. This sign tells you a flagger is ahead. Obey all the flagger's directions.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to get ready to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before you turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents another car from pushing you into oncoming traffic if it hits you from behind.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a regular vehicle.
They brake more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a regular vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. Following too closely is dangerous for you and the rider. You need space and time to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly.

questions.question: When passing another car, when do you have enough space to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to move back.
When you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure there is enough space between your car and the other car. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows your thinking and body functions. It reduces your ability to concentrate and stay alert.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or slope.
When parked on the side of a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or slope.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. This prevents you from entering traffic if hit from behind. When parked on a hill or slope, turn your wheels away from the road. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: After passing a car, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are far enough from the car you passed. Check your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
More slowly than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter a freeway at or near the speed of traffic. Only go slower if traffic is already speeding above the legal limit.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles. Other drivers also have trouble seeing you in these conditions.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means passing is allowed on that side. A solid yellow line means passing is not allowed on that side.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to get ready to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast on your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast on your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast when danger is near. Do this if a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your moving car.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
Passing on the right is allowed when the road is clear.
Passing on the left is allowed when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is allowed when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can pass another car on the left when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Which medications can affect a driver's ability to drive?

options.text: Only sleeping pills
Any medication
Only illegal drugs

questions.correctAnswerText: Any medication
questions.explanation: Do not drive when taking new medication until you know it will not affect your driving. You cannot drive under the influence of any controlled drug. This is dangerous and is a crime called Driving While Under the Influence (DWUI).

questions.question: How can you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. To check your blind spots, look over your shoulders.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot affect driving ability if taken as directed.
Any medication prescribed by a doctor is safe to take anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications—both prescription and over-the-counter—can be dangerous and may affect your driving. Cold and allergy medications can make you drowsy and impact your ability to drive safely. You are responsible for knowing how your medication affects your driving.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after stopping completely.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means traffic cannot move in the direction the arrow shows. You must stop and wait for a green signal before moving in that direction.

questions.question: If a police officer directs you to drive through a red light, you should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Always follow police officer instructions over traffic signals and signs. A police officer directing traffic has authority over all traffic rules.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces all the abilities you need to drive safely. It enters your stomach, then your blood, then your entire body. Alcohol first affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car slide to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: Is a driver license a right or a privilege?

options.text: A right, not a privilege.
A privilege, not a right.
A requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by following the rules.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your horn?

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians because it may be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or let you pass, even if you use your turn signal. The space you want may not be free.

questions.question: Roads become slippery when rain first starts. When the road is slippery, you should:

options.text: Avoid making turns and stops while driving fast.
Test your tires' grip while going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making turns and stops while driving fast.
questions.explanation: A wet, slippery road reduces your tires' grip. You must drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. Avoid fast turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match your speed to other traffic, signal, and:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in because you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to be empty before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, and signal. Then merge safely into the gap. Stay alert and do not expect other drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your brain and body. It weakens your judgment and makes your reactions slower.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right, you should:

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Watch for on-ramps ahead. When safe, move to the left lane to give vehicles room to enter from the on-ramp on your right.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the back wheels follow a tighter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need more space to turn right and may swing wide.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and go carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: In very foggy conditions, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam lights.
Use your low beam lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam lights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway, drivers:

options.text: May continue driving.
Must stop until the school bus starts moving.
Must stop until the stop arm goes up.

questions.correctAnswerText: May continue driving.
questions.explanation: If a divided highway separates you from the school bus, you may keep driving. If there is no divider, drivers on both sides must stop.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of two lanes going your direction. Many cars are passing you on the right. If the driver behind you wants to go faster, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane to drive slower than traffic, enter the road, or turn right.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming lights are blinding, look at the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This keeps your car on the road until the other car passes.
